                    Calculating Sums and Scalar Multiplication of Vectors Given in Alternative Notation
canonical_examples.problem:
The vectors $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are given in the picture below. Find the coordinates of $\vec{a}+6\vec{b}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252434/assets/56b10e759084da6fb21c8421bc9ff6d74aac2602df28f6c8e478bd874d7d6e9f.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
From the picture, we obtain $\vec{a}=\langle -3,2 \rangle$ and $\vec{b}=\langle 4,5 \rangle.$

Therefore, to compute the result, we just need to perform the required operations with each component separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{a}+6\overset{\to }{b} & =⟨-3,2⟩+6\cdot ⟨4,5⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,2⟩+⟨6\cdot 4,6\cdot 5⟩ \\  & =⟨-3,2⟩+⟨24,30⟩ \\  & =⟨21,32⟩\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.problem:
Suppose we are given two vectors 
$\mathbf{a} = \langle 2,3 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{b} = \langle -4,4 \rangle,$ shown below. How do we compute the vectors $\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b}$  and  $-5\mathbf{a}$ in terms of the standard basis $\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252434/assets/254809cbc834b493759a6fa09222a2c90c5fbfc3280d22e82470e760a7a4c508.png)

To compute $\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b},$ we collect all of the $\mathbf{i}$'s and $\mathbf{j}$'s. We know that $\mathbf{a} = {\color{red}2}\mathbf{i} + {\color{blue}3}\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{b} = {\color{red}-4}\mathbf{i} + {\color{blue}4}\mathbf{j}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}a+b & =(2i+3j)+(-4i+4j) \\  & =(2+(-4))i+(3+4)j \\  & =-2i+7j.\end{aligned}
$$

Writing our answer in angle bracket and column vector notations, we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252434/assets/eae25a74dde73f7899f6ccbbdbb1a1f589fc72cad9629a33b4fdbbbc753efcd8.svg)

To compute $-5\mathbf{a},$ we multiply each of the components by $-5\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}-5\cdot a & =-5(2i+3j) \\  & =(-5\cdot 2)i+(-5\cdot 3)j \\  & =-10i+-15j\end{aligned}
$$

Writing our answer in angle bracket and column vector notations, we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252434/assets/05f847a73201db3de20db3847ef4ed97e07ea7fae9325401b1ea5a460968f9da.svg)

tutorials.title: Introduction
tutorials.content:
Suppose we are given two vectors 
$\mathbf{a} = \langle 2,3 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{b} = \langle -4,4 \rangle,$ shown below. How do we compute the vectors $\mathbf{a} + \mathbf{b}$  and  $-5\mathbf{a}$ in terms of the standard basis $\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252434/assets/254809cbc834b493759a6fa09222a2c90c5fbfc3280d22e82470e760a7a4c508.png)

To compute $\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b},$ we collect all of the $\mathbf{i}$'s and $\mathbf{j}$'s. We know that $\mathbf{a} = {\color{red}2}\mathbf{i} + {\color{blue}3}\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{b} = {\color{red}-4}\mathbf{i} + {\color{blue}4}\mathbf{j}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}a+b & =(2i+3j)+(-4i+4j) \\  & =(2+(-4))i+(3+4)j \\  & =-2i+7j.\end{aligned}
$$

Writing our answer in angle bracket and column vector notations, we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252434/assets/eae25a74dde73f7899f6ccbbdbb1a1f589fc72cad9629a33b4fdbbbc753efcd8.svg)

To compute $-5\mathbf{a},$ we multiply each of the components by $-5\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}-5\cdot a & =-5(2i+3j) \\  & =(-5\cdot 2)i+(-5\cdot 3)j \\  & =-10i+-15j\end{aligned}
$$

Writing our answer in angle bracket and column vector notations, we get 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252434/assets/05f847a73201db3de20db3847ef4ed97e07ea7fae9325401b1ea5a460968f9da.svg)

tutorials.name: Sums and Scalar Multiplication of Vectors in Angle Bracket or Column Vector Form
tutorials.problem:
To add or subtract vectors given in angle bracket or column vector form, we just need to add or subtract each component separately.

For example, in angle bracket notation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨2,5⟩+⟨-3,7⟩ & = \\ ⟨2+(-3),5+7⟩ & = \\ ⟨-1,12⟩ & ,\end{aligned}
$$

and in column vector notation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 7\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2+(-3) \\ 5+7\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 12\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Likewise, to multiply a vector given in angle bracket or column vector form, we just need to multiply each component separately.

For example, in angle bracket notation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-5\cdot ⟨2,5⟩ & = \\ ⟨(-5)\cdot 2,(-5)\cdot 5⟩ & = \\ ⟨-10,-25⟩ & ,\end{aligned}
$$

and in column vector notation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-5\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}(-5)\cdot 2 \\ (-5)\cdot 5\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ -25\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: Common Notations Used When Describing Vectors
tutorials.problem:
To denote a vector, we have used two notations:

- a single bold lowercase letter, such as $\mathbf{v},$ or

- two uppercase letters representing the points of the ends of the vector, with an arrow over them, such as $\overrightarrow{AB}.$

We will mostly stick to these notations. However, there are many possible notations for vectors. For example, sometimes a vector can be denoted as

$$
\vec{v}, \quad \overrightarrow{V}, \quad v, \quad \hat{v}.
$$

The rightmost notation, $\hat{v},$ is usually used to represent unit vectors in particular.
